title: Obsidian Security hits a $1.1bn valuation as AI reshapes the threat
excerpt: SaaS-security firm Obsidian has raised fresh funding at a $1.1bn valuation as demand surges for tools that secure AI agents inside enterprise apps.
content_html:
Obsidian Security has become the latest cybersecurity company to be repriced upward by artificial intelligence. The SaaS-security firm has raised a fresh funding of $85 Million Series D at a $1.1bn valuation as demand for tools that secure AI surges.

The raise pushes Obsidian into unicorn territory and reflects a simple dynamic. Every new way that companies use AI is also a new way for them to be attacked, and someone has to guard it.

Investors have clearly noticed the gap. Money has poured into startups securing enterprise AI, from Onyx’s $113m round to keep humans in control of AI agents to a string of others racing to build the same guardrails.

Obsidian, founded in 2017, made its name protecting software-as-a-service applications, the sprawl of cloud tools like Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and Workday that hold a modern company’s data.

Its systems watch for compromised accounts, risky configurations, and identity-based attacks across that estate.

The problem it started with has only grown. A large company now runs hundreds of SaaS applications, each a door into its data, and most security teams struggle to see across all of them at once.

Identity has become the real battleground. As the perimeter dissolved into the cloud, attackers stopped breaking in and started logging in, using stolen credentials and over-permissioned accounts, exactly the weakness AI agents now multiply.

The pitch has now tilted toward AI. Obsidian has been building defences for the AI agents that companies are plugging into their SaaS tools, software that can read, write, and act on corporate data with far less oversight than a human employee.

That autonomy is the whole worry. An agent handed broad access to a company’s applications is powerful and dangerous in equal measure, and a single misconfigured or hijacked agent can reach data no phishing email ever could.

The speed is what changes the maths. A compromised employee clicks a few wrong links; a compromised agent can move across dozens of apps and touch enormous volumes of data before anyone notices.

Obsidian’s advantage is that it already sits inside the SaaS layer where much of this plays out. Securing AI agents is, in large part, about controlling what they can touch, and Obsidian has spent years mapping exactly that.

The timing suits the money. Agentic AI adoption has accelerated inside enterprises, and security budgets tend to follow new technology once the first breaches make the risk feel concrete.

The bigger players are buying in, too. Databricks recently acquired Panther Labs in a cybersecurity push, a sign that AI-era security is becoming a category the giants want to own rather than partner for.

Obsidian has raised from a roster of well-known investors over the years, including Greylock, Wing, GV, and Norwest, and the new valuation marks a sharp step up from its earlier rounds.

The company has been signalling the shift in its own product line, rolling out AI-agent defences and SaaS supply-chain protection as agentic adoption picks up. The funding is the market’s endorsement of that direction.

Security has been one of the few software categories where AI clearly adds demand rather than threatening it. The same automation that unnerves defenders is also creating the work that keeps companies like Obsidian growing.

Valuations in security have run hot before, and not every AI-security startup will grow into its price. The wager is that securing AI becomes as unavoidable as securing email once did.

For Obsidian, the $1.1bn tag is a bet by investors that the SaaS security problem and the AI security problem are becoming the same problem. If they are right, the company spent a decade preparing for a market that has only just arrived.

content_html_zh:
Obsidian Security 成为最新一家通过人工智能重新定价的网络安全公司。 随着对人工智能安全工具的需求激增，这家 SaaS 安全公司以 11 亿美元的估值筹集了 8500 万美元的 D 轮新资金。

这次融资将 Obsidian 推向了独角兽领域，并反映出一种简单的动态。 企业使用人工智能的每一种新方式也是他们受到攻击的一种新方式，必须有人来防范。

投资者已经清楚地注意到了这一差距。 大量资金涌入确保企业人工智能安全的初创公司，从 Onyx 的 1.13 亿美元融资，让人类控制人工智能代理，到一系列其他公司竞相构建相同的护栏。

Obsidian 成立于 2017 年，因保护软件即服务应用程序而闻名，这些应用程序是保存现代公司数据的 Salesforce、Microsoft 365 和 Workday 等庞大的云工具。

其系统监视整个资产中的受损帐户、危险配置和基于身份的攻击。

一开始的问题只会越来越严重。 一家大公司现在运行数百个 SaaS 应用程序，每个应用程序都可以访问其数据，大多数安全团队很难同时查看所有这些应用程序。

身份已成为真正的战场。 随着边界融入云中，攻击者停止入侵并开始使用窃取的凭据和过度许可的帐户进行登录，这正是人工智能代理现在的弱点正在成倍增加。

现在，焦点已经转向人工智能。 Obsidian 一直在为 AI 代理构建防御措施，公司将这些代理插入到 SaaS 工具中，这些软件可以读取、写入和处理公司数据，而受到的监督远少于人类员工。

这种自主权就是全部的担忧。 授予对公司应用程序的广泛访问权限的代理既强大又危险，而且单个配置错误或被劫持的代理可以访问网络钓鱼电子邮件无法访问的数据。

速度改变了数学。 受感染的员工点击了一些错误的链接；受感染的代理可以在数十个应用程序之间移动，并在任何人注意到之前接触大量数据。

Obsidian 的优势在于它已经位于 SaaS 层中，其中大部分内容都在该层中发挥作用。 确保人工智能代理的安全在很大程度上是为了控制他们可以接触的内容，而 Obsidian 多年来一直在准确地描绘这一点。

时机适合金钱。 代理人工智能在企业内部的采用加速了，一旦第一次泄露使风险变得具体，安全预算往往会遵循新技术。

更大的参与者也在买入。 Databricks 最近在网络安全推动中收购了 Panther Labs，这表明人工智能时代的安全正在成为巨头们想要拥有而不是合作的一个类别。

多年来，Obsidian 从 Greylock、Wing、GV 和 Norwest 等知名投资者那里筹集了资金，新的估值标志着其前几轮融资的大幅提升。

该公司一直在暗示自己的产品线将发生转变，随着代理采用的增加，推出了人工智能代理防御和 SaaS 供应链保护。 资金是市场对该方向的认可。

安全性是人工智能明显增加而非威胁需求的少数几个软件类别之一。 同样让防御者感到不安的自动化也创造了让像 Obsidian 这样的公司不断成长的工作。

安全领域的估值此前曾一度炙手可热，但并不是每家人工智能安全初创公司都能增长到其股价。 可以肯定的是，保护人工智能的安全将变得像保护电子邮件的安全一样不可避免。

对于 Obsidian 来说，11 亿美元的标签是投资者押注 SaaS 安全问题和 AI 安全问题正在成为同一个问题。 如果他们是对的，那么该公司花了十年时间为刚刚到来的市场做准备。
